source_review.notes: Checked the primary MapReduce, RDD, unreliable-failure-detector, Borg, and DieHard papers plus current official Flink and Kubernetes documentation and Google SRE guidance. Sources support task/lineage recovery, suspicion under timing uncertainty, correlated placement, checkpoint/local-state assumptions, heartbeat observations, and retry/overload cascades. All ten URLs returned HTTP 200 on the retrieval date.

evidence: Reviewed failure-assumption tuple, replica-loss events, general and independent availability expressions, quorum formula, shared-domain conditional model, suspicion predicate, surviving-state/work sets, and backlog catch-up equation.
Checked event complements, intersections, conditional scope, binomial coefficient for two-or-more live replicas, and rate dimensions.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Availability, durability, job success, safety, liveness, suspicion, and recovery completion remain distinct.

evidence: Executed correlated-failure-arithmetic with Python 3.14.4 and reproduced every exact fraction and six-decimal value for independent workers, one shared zone, independent zones, quorum, and overstatement.
Recomputed exercise values as 0.999875 independent availability, 0.98987625 shared-rack availability, and 0.00999875 overstatement.
Recomputed catch-up as 960 GB divided by 4 GB/min equals 240 minutes plus eight-minute restore equals 248 minutes.
numerical_recomputation.notes: Probabilities are exact only within declared toy models and are not forecasts for real clusters.

evidence: Derived at-least-one availability from the complement of joint loss and reduced it to one minus the product only under independence.
Derived three-replica quorum availability as all three live plus exactly two live and conditioned both availability forms on shared-domain survival.
Derived finite catch-up only for service rate greater than arrival rate and separated suspicion from crash truth.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: Correlation, interval, repair, stationary behavior, and dependency availability are explicit assumptions rather than hidden constants.

evidence: Reviewed process pause/crash/restart, host and local-disk loss, asymmetric partitions, delayed messages, corrupt state, false suspicion, old-actor resumption, control-plane loss, credential expiry, and hostile behavior exclusions.
Reviewed one/many replicas, same-host/rack/zone placement, cross-zone shared dependencies, global rollout/schema/operator error, load transfer, restore traffic, retry waves, and zero spare capacity.

Reviewed missing/partial/incompatible checkpoints, source retention gaps, sink acknowledgement loss, nondeterministic replay, stale generations, backlog rates at less/equal/greater than arrival, and regional public-service degradation.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Physical, logical, administrative, software, storage, dependency, and human common causes are separately represented.

evidence: Traced detector ambiguity, authority fencing, attempt/generation isolation, state-survival matrix, placement domains, retry classification, post-failure capacity, RPO/RTO, and retained evidence through exposition and exercises.
Checked that local state is secondary for host-loss models and complete recovery depends on compatible checkpoint metadata, replayable sources, accessible dependencies, and sink semantics.
Checked that numerical availability never appears without scenario and correlation caveats.
invariant_checking.notes: The chapter does not infer death from silence, independence from labels, durability from replica count, or recovery from process restart.

evidence: Reviewed all ten recovery-claim obligations from visible service contract through residual fault review.

Checked counterexamples for timeout-proves-crash, replica-count-equals-domains, availability-equals-durability, component-percentage multiplication, checkpoint-file-equals-recoverability, retry-everything, lease-expiry-equals-fencing, and restart-equals-RTO claims.
Reviewed safety under false suspicion, liveness under real failure, conditional availability, state reconstruction, restore/catch-up, and test-evidence arguments.
proof_review.notes: Fault model, probability, protocol safety, operational liveness, measurement, and domain approval remain independent evidence obligations.

evidence: Audited uses of prove, guarantee, independent, conditional, available, durable, authoritative, safe, exactly-once, and recovered.
Confirmed toy calculations and successful drills are explicitly scoped and do not claim universal availability or independence.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Current product behaviors are tied to cited documentation and retrieval date.

evidence: Reviewed source dates, arithmetic-fixture scope, required topology/state/detector/recovery evidence, trial conditions, observation windows, denominators, distributions, and incident feedback.
Confirmed no real-cluster availability, disaster-recovery attainment, public-safety assurance, certification, or external-review claim is made.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: Production claims require exact topology, dependencies, observed fault/repair behavior, repeated failure trials, capacity/load, output reconciliation, and objective attainment.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed faults, errors, failures, observations, modes, detectors, fencing, domains, correlation, state survival, dataflow recovery, retry, capacity, objectives, and tests as one coherent assumption model.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed detector tuning, topology audits, state-survival matrices, failure classification, stage/checkpoint generations, sink fencing, restore bandwidth, retry budgets, backlog catch-up, failure injection, abort criteria, and operational evidence. Internal practitioner-oriented review only.

pedagogical_review.notes: Verified progression from fault vocabulary through detection, correlation, state, recovery, capacity, objectives, and drills; ten examples and five complete answers cover calculation, modeling, diagnosis, design, and unfamiliar public-benefits transfer.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external reliability researcher, distributed-runtime practitioner, platform provider, public-safety specialist, benefits-policy expert, ethics/fairness reviewer, or certification review is claimed.
